name: ball-on-ramp
assumptions: Drawing has no numeric dimensions, so scale is inferred: ground line at y=0, ramp is a right-triangular prism about 4 m wide (slope run) by 2 m tall with 0.6 m depth in Z. Gravity is Earth-like (0,-9.81,0). The ramp and ground are fixed structural supports; the ball is a loose dynamic sphere. No motion or actuation is requested, so all bodies start at rest and no motors/forces are added. The ball is treated as a solid rigid sphere (no rolling constraint beyond contact).
warnings: The drawn stroke thickness is decorative and not modeled as a separate physical thickness. The ball contact on the sloped face is handled by stackAbove vertical contact; initial placement is near the top corner as drawn.
message: Built a rigid display/physics model of a ball at the top of an inclined ramp on fixed ground. No requested motion, so nothing is actuated.

grounding.note: Horizontal ground line along the bottom of the sketch.
Right-triangular ramp: vertical left side, sloped face down to the right, bottom edge on the ground.
Circle resting at the top corner where the vertical side meets the sloped face.
